canonical_statement: For every integer n at least 3 and every smooth compactly supported real-valued function u on R^n, the integral of |u(x)|^2 / |x|^2 is at most (2/(n-2))^2 times the integral of the squared Euclidean norm of the gradient of u.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat with 3 <= n; u : C_c^infinity(R^n, R); all mathematical objects intended in Lean universe levels determined by the eventual encoding
ordered_binders: u : smooth compactly supported function (Fin n -> Real) -> Real
conclusion: integral x, |u x|^2 / ||x||^2 <= (2/(n-2))^2 * integral x, ||gradient u x||^2
boundary_and_degenerate_cases: Dimensions n = 0, 1, 2 are excluded. The value of the singular integrand at x = 0 is measure-theoretically irrelevant but its encoding must be fixed during statement work. u = 0 is included.
